items.summary: Microsoft warned that attackers exploited a flaw in its cloud-based Entra Connect Health monitoring service to gain unauthorized read-only access to administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information, though no passwords or authentication tokens were compromised. The vulnerability was first introduced on July 23, 2026, discovered by Microsoft on November 9 after it confirmed exploitation, with the investigation concluding on November 20 that only metadata had been accessed without any unauthorized configuration changes; a server-side fix deployed on November 19 required no customer remediation. Exposed data included technical contact and administrator email addresses, tenant IDs and regional details, license tiers, directory synchronization status, Connect Health onboarding state, and an expired certificate previously used to register agents with a decommissioned internal service that remained in storage and was still returned by the API; passwords, cryptographic keys, Active Directory topology, and Azure subscription information were not exposed. Microsoft reviewed telemetry for unauthorized API calls but did not disclose how many organizations or tenants were affected—though more than a dozen administrators reported receiving notifications, some MSPs received alerts spanning multiple customer tenants hours apart—and declined to identify who exploited the flaw or when attacks began; it recommended phishing-resistant multifactor authentication and log reviews while publishing a PowerShell script that displays current configuration values rather than what was accessed during the breach. These details are drawn from Microsoft's notification as relayed in a Reddit post, corroborated by BleepingComputer contact with Microsoft, though impact scope remains unconfirmed.
items.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health vulnerability exposed tenant metadata

items.summary: Tesla began rolling out Full Self-Driving (FSD) version 15 on X, accompanied by release notes from the Tesla Super Intelligence account. The update upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network, including an upgraded vision encoder shared with Robotaxi and Optimus that is trained on millions of internet videos for improved generalization and data efficiency; a new visualization called 'Tesla Augmented Reality' (marketed as 'Reality View') that replaces all explicit model signals with a single end-to-end visualization using less compute; improved navigation based on an end-to-end learned model from route preference data; personalized parking location selection showing multiple options at the destination; and better driver monitoring. Tesla claims the new vision encoder improves the critical intervention rate by 25x, but does not publish the underlying number or disengagement data that would verify it. The release notes also list improved detection of road signs, small animals, debris, chains, potholes, deep standing water, speed handling for each driver profile and school zones, slowing for speed cameras, Bike Rack Mode, and navigation learning covering only trip start and end for now, with later v15 releases planned to expand it. The article notes that almost every driving improvement targets an area where FSD currently struggles: a September test by Brussels nonprofit Johanna.be found FSD exceeded the limit in 55% of the 30 km/h zones it drove through, averaging 44 km/h while its screen showed a 50 km/h limit; Musk said pothole avoidance was 'coming soon' back in 2019 but FSD still drives straight through them today; and NHTSA is reviewing a petition about Robotaxi speeds in active school zones alongside an investigation opened October 2025 into traffic-law violations. The article also flags one change that goes the other way: Tesla says it is decreasing strictness of driver monitoring in higher-speed profiles, even as sleeping drivers on FSD keep making headlines and Europe tightens monitoring at regulators' request. It notes v14 arrived in October 2025 with hallucinations, brake stabbing, and excessive speeding (early crowdsourced data showed about 732 miles between critical disengagements), improved later, then regressed before Musk sold v14.3 as the version where 'the last big piece of the puzzle finally lands.' The article concludes that while the visuals are impressive and could make FSD easier to supervise, whether v15 delivers real progress on detection remains unverified because Tesla still won't publish disengagement data, and it has a history of point releases breaking things. An unrelated EnergySage advertisement appears at the end.
items.title: Tesla rolls out FSD v15 with claims of a 25x safety improvement and new 'Reality View' visualization, targeting its biggest weaknesses: sign detection, potholes, school zones, and speed handling

items.summary: Tesla is rolling out a software update that makes the Cybertruck turn even tighter, improving on an already competitive curb-to-curb turning circle. The maneuverability comes from rear-wheel steering paired with steer-by-wire: at low speeds the rear wheels turn opposite to the fronts, shrinking the space needed for a U-turn. Tesla's owner's manual lists the current turning circle at about 43.5 ft (13.25 m), which beats the Ford F-150 Lightning at roughly 47.8 ft and the Rivian R1T at 44.9 ft, and is within about 4 ft of a Model Y for a truck weighing about 6,600 lb and measuring nearly 19 feet long. At launch the rear wheels turned only about 3 degrees; in early 2024 an engineer said a software update would push that to 10 degrees, though Tesla has not confirmed whether this rollout delivers the full amount or why it is limited to model year 2027 trucks—likely because earlier hardware may be incompatible. The improvement requires software version 2026.44 or newer and applies only to model year 2027 Cybertrucks, which Tesla plans to stop building by end of summer 2027 as it shifts production toward the Cybercab; at that point only the $109,990 Cyberbeast remains available. The article notes this update does not address factors cited for weak sales—pricing far above the ~$40,000 promised in 2019 (the current model is priced well above it), and range and towing that fell short.
items.title: Tesla Rolls Out Tighter-Turning Cybertruck Update for Final Model Year

visual.alt: Dot chart. turning circle at about 43.5 ft; Lightning 47.8 ft; T 44.9 ft.

items.summary: A Hindi news roundup presents five top stories without a single unifying event. The lead item reports that Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah is arriving on his first bilateral visit to India on [d1: 22 November], where he will meet PM Narendra Modi and Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar; Nepal seeks more than $2 billion in economic assistance from India, though the specific agenda topics are not detailed beyond these meetings. A separate item attributes an estimate that India-Italy bilateral trade could exceed €50 billion by [d1: 2035] to ASSOCHAM, with potential benefits for automotive, pharma and technology sectors; this is a projection rather than a confirmed figure. The third story states that Bollywood actor Amir Khan has rented three luxury apartments in Santa Cruz West, Mumbai, at an initial monthly rent of ₹38 lakh, totaling roughly ₹19.65 crore over four years. A fourth item reports Vedanta chairman Anil Agarwal's proposal to increase jobs and salaries after questions from PM Modi about privatization of government companies, claiming it could create millions of jobs and multiply production—attributed entirely to his claim without independent verification. The fifth story describes new allegations that Nvidia's board was upset over Jensen Huang concealing details of a reported affair before he resigned; Trump, Musk and thousands of employees reportedly want him back while the board opposes reappointment. No limitations or caveats are stated in the source beyond these attributions to individuals or organizations.
items.title: Five Top Stories Cover Nepal PM's India Visit, India-Italy Trade Outlook, Amir Khan Rental Deal and Nvidia Dispute
